snippet.text: [Issue #636](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/636) found that a host round on [pull request #532](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/532) ran with its Codex login at its usage limit: every lens moved to Claude, but triage and the walkthrough asked only their first model, so every lens ran at its default level and the walkthrough was a fixed note, with nothing in the verdict to say so. Triage's `RouteTextModel` and the walkthrough's `SummaryTask` now move along their route by the lens rule, `isFailoverError`. A triage decision records the model that answered and those that refused before it, a verdict whose triage answered on no model prints a `Reach:` line, and the walkthrough records the models by name alone. No stored shape takes a new version, and neither key changes what it matches; [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-22-triage-and-the-walkthrough-fail-over.md) and the [identity guideline](../guidelines/identity.md) rows say why. Before the fix, the four triage tests failed on `9ffc8330d` and the four walkthrough tests failed with `expected [ 'scripted' ] to deeply equal [ 'scripted', 'other' ]`. The mutant inventory, [2026-11-22-issue-636-triage-failover-mutants.json](2026-11-22-issue-636-triage-failover-mutants.json), covers `packages/core/src/decider.ts`, `packages/pipeline/src/models.ts`, `packages/decisions/src/fallback.ts` and `packages/pipeline/src/summarize.ts`: 163 generated mutants, 132 killed by tests of the first two commits, 20 by tests added for survivors, and 11 equivalent, each with its reason. Every named test passed unmutated, then failed alone with its mutant applied, in [the recorded runs](2026-11-22-issue-636-triage-failover-mutant-runs.json): the first run at `d1d9c09cb`, the survivors' reruns with the tests committed at `0845fce5c`. Three mutants that empty or never leave the walkthrough's loop hung their test alone for 120 seconds; the runner stopped each by its recorded pids and left none running. snippet.text: A lens, its planner and prober, and the verifier move to the next model of their route when a model fails in a way another provider would not. That is a transient failure, a failed login, a usage limit, or, from 2026-11-20, a provider's content filter refusing what the model was sent. A filter refusal moves only to a model the route holds, so inside a guarded `accept` it stays inside it. The lens's record says which models refused the content and which answered, so a reader tells a refusal from a limit, and a lens whose every model refused fails with a reason that says so. From 2026-11-22, triage and the walkthrough move along their route by the same rule. A triage decision records which models refused and which answered, a review whose triage answered on no model says so in a caveat its verdict prints, and the walkthrough records the models by name alone, by [the decision](decisions/2026-11-22-triage-and-the-walkthrough-fail-over.md). [The refusal decision](decisions/2026-11-20-content-filter-refusal-fails-over.md) records what this gives up: a change's content can now decide which accepted model reviews it.

snippet.text: | Triage request, producer `triage` | `pipeline/src/triage-request.ts` | attaches to a recorded triage decision | The real request, under `nonce`. The key holds the decider's name and version, the question set, the questions, the input-cut flag and the state rendered under a fixed nonce. The flag is set when either the change under the fixed nonce or the decider's copy under `nonce` is cut, since quoting shortens a change that holds the fixed nonce; it can then differ between two reviews of one change, which only re-asks triage. The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437). The model that answered and the models that refused before it, which the decision stores as `model` and `refused`: they are the answer's, not the request's, so the key still comes from the request alone. The decider's name names the route's head, `llm-fallback:<head>`, and any model the route accepts may answer its question. So a decision a fallback answered while the head was at its limit is reused once the head is back, by the coordinator's answer of 2026-11-22 on [issue #636](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/636) |
